title: Refresh streaming + tool calling examples; add structured output sample and safer error handling
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: Python SDK: refreshed copy/paste examples for streaming + tool calling; added structured output (JSON schema) sample and improved error handling guidance for stream disconnects and partial tool args.
description: Summary: This PR refreshes the Python SDK’s developer-facing examples to match the current canonical patterns for (1) streaming response consumption, (2) tool/function calling semantics, and (3) structured output constrained by JSON schema. Motivation: Support and Solutions Engineering have repeatedly flagged confusion around partial tool-call arguments mid-stream (SUP-18421) and structured output occasionally producing invalid JSON if users attempt to parse before completion (SUP-18436). The previous snippets also differed from TS/Go conventions (event naming, final assembly rules), leading to copy/paste failures and inconsistent mental models. What changed (examples + ergonomics only): Streaming: Updated streaming loop to explicitly handle delta vs final events, assemble final message content deterministically, and log event types for debugging. Added a recommended pattern for handling disconnects (graceful cancel + retry from last user message rather than trying to “resume” a stream). Tool calling: Updated tool definitions to match current supported semantics (name/description/parameters JSON schema). Updated the agent loop to support multiple tool calls in a single assistant turn, including parallel execution guidance. Added explicit handling for partial tool-call arguments during streaming: buffer tool-call argument deltas and only json.loads() once a tool call is marked final. Structured output: Added a new runnable sample demonstrating schema-constrained output with JSON schema validation and a safe fallback path (retry with tighter instruction if validation fails). Clarified that streaming + structured output requires waiting for the final event before parsing/validating. Error handling: Standardized exception handling across examples (timeouts, API errors, KeyboardInterrupt) and improved user-facing console output. Included a small helper for consistent printing of tool calls + results in transcripts. Notes on API compatibility: No protocol changes are introduced here; this is an examples refresh plus small helper utilities used only by examples. Examples are written to work on the latest released redwood-sdk-python version on main; no unreleased APIs required. Checklist: [x] Examples run end-to-end with REDWOOD_API_KEY set [x] Aligns with DevEx streaming event conventions and tool-calling parity guidelines [x] Includes structured output schema + validation [x] Adds tests for example transcript stability (lightweight) [x] Docs/comments updated to discourage incremental JSON parsing mid-stream
commits: examples: refresh streaming consumer loop to assemble deltas/final message deterministically
examples: update tool calling sample to support multi-tool calls and tool-result messages
examples: add structured output (JSON schema) sample with validation + retry guidance
examples: standardize error handling/logging and improve README copy/paste steps
tests: add minimal snapshot-style transcript checks for examples

Sabrina James (author): Good call — updated comments and added a buffer dict keyed by tool_call_id; parsing only happens on tool_call.final. Brian Murphy (review): For structured output, can we show a validation failure path that doesn’t just “trust the model”? I’d like to see a retry with a tighter instruction + an explicit schema validation error printed. Sabrina James (author): Added validate_or_retry() helper in the structured output example; on ValidationError we print the error, add a corrective system note, and retry once with the same schema. Wei Chen (review): README needs to make it obvious which model to use and that structured output guarantees vary by model family. Sabrina James (author): Updated README wording to say “pick a model that supports schema-constrained output” and included a note about checking the docs support matrix; also added a fallback section explaining what to do when the model can’t comply. Monica Patel (review): Please keep helper utilities scoped to examples only; don’t expand the public surface area in this PR. Sabrina James (author): Confirmed: helpers live under examples/ and are not exported; no changes to SDK client API. Monica Patel (approval): Approved after last round; thanks for keeping parity with TS/Go and addressing SUP-18421 explicitly.
